summary: Verified the HR login bug fix. Idempotent startup seeding in server.py no longer overwrites existing role-account passwords. Backend regression (pytest, 10 tests) passes 100%: HR logs in with new password 'Hr@BankEzee@$', old seeded 'HrNeo12!!' is rejected, admin/manager/ops/GP still log in, wrong/unknown creds return 401, and HR still logs in after a fresh `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` (persistence proven). UI test at /login for HR redirected to /agent/attendance successfully.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py still writes `plain_password` (cleartext) for freshly-seeded/reseeded role accounts. Storing plaintext passwords alongside the bcrypt hash is a security smell; consider removing the `plain_password` field entirely and relying only on the hash + Admin change-password flow.
The seeding loop uses hard-coded credentials in ROLE_ACCOUNTS in source. Move to environment variables (or a one-time bootstrap script) so secrets are not committed.
test_credentials: Used credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md; HR = hr@neosales.in / Hr@BankEzee@$ (new). No credentials modified during testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The login regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_login_regression.py covers HR bug + role-account logins + negative cases. Reuse it after any auth/seeding changes. Backend was restarted once during testing to prove password persistence.
rca of the issue: RCA (confirmed): setup_admin_accounts() startup hook previously did unconditional update_one($set password=hash(hardcoded), plain_password=...) for every ROLE_ACCOUNTS entry, so any Admin-driven password change was reverted on every restart. Fix: password fields are only written when the account is missing entirely, has no credential, or RESEED_ROLE_PASSWORDS=true is set. Verified idempotency by restarting backend and confirming HR still authenticates with the new password while the old seed value returns 401.
